Fixture: 15_modular_rgb_600x520_multisection_lossless.jxl
600x520 RGB, mathematically lossless -- multi-section TOC, RGB variant of 14

Purpose
-------
Targets slice 7's unproven multi-section path (Annex G / F.3), same as
14_modular_gray_600x520_multisection_lossless.jxl.txt -- see that sidecar for
the full rationale on why 07-13 never reach `num_sections > 1` and why
600x520 does. This fixture is the RGB counterpart: same canvas, same
gradient formula as 09/11/13 (R ramps x, G ramps y, B is a diagonal
sawtooth), so it exercises multi-section tiling TOGETHER WITH the RCT
(reversible colour transform) and per-group entropy-decoder state across
three colour channels and 9 groups -- 14 deliberately keeps those concerns
separate (single channel, no RCT) to isolate multi-section handling first;
this fixture is the "both at once" check.

This gradient compresses far better than the diagonal-ramp grayscale content
of 14 (smooth per-channel ramps vs. a mod-256 sawtooth on chroma), which is
why the fixture is only ~1.3 KB despite covering the same pixel count as 14
(18.8 KB) -- effort/entropy-coding behaviour, not a different image size.

Provenance
----------
  Encoder:      cjxl v0.13.0 196a43d9 [_AVX2_,SSE4,SSE2] {GNU 15.2.0}
  libjxl rev:   196a43d996aa6ed33ebf98812a7c6d43b2b6d01b (v0.12-snapshot-2-g196a43d9)
  cjxl flags:   -d 0 -e 7
  Built by:     tools/setup-oracles.sh (flags recorded in
                tools/oracle-bin/PINNED_REVISIONS.txt)
  Regenerate:   tools/make-modular-fixtures.sh
                That script IS the recipe; it rewrites the source and re-encodes.

  Source image: tests/fixtures/generated/src_rgb_600x520.ppm  (936015 bytes)
                sha256 7c3659b222731015fa351feb88c1e3c1b9c176ea23a8ad785b4f2f110f832876
                Synthetic, written by the Python snippet inside
                tools/make-modular-fixtures.sh -- no third-party image was
                used, converted, or consulted. 600x520 8-bit RGB (PPM P6):
                  R = x * 255 / 599     ramp along x
                  G = y * 255 / 519     ramp along y
                  B = (x + y) mod 256   diagonal sawtooth
                Same gradient family as 09/11/13.

  Fixture:      1252 bytes
                sha256 e823e05801b0dd97973ef8407a6f99a7c6964587f7df4a1ec6a4dfb94bb987b4

Verification
------------
djxl decodes it to a PPM byte-identical to the source (checked on every run
of tools/make-modular-fixtures.sh). Classified by `jpxl info` (jpxl-cli) as
a recognized "naked codestream", 1252 bytes.

Independently, this crate's own `FrameGeometry::from_header` + `read_toc`
report `group_dim = 256`, `num_groups = 9`, `num_sections = 12` for this
fixture, same geometry as 14 (identical canvas size) -- see
tests/e2e_multisection.rs.

Modular features engaged
-------------------------
Multi-section tiling, same as 14 (2 header sections + 1 LF group + 9 pass
groups), forced by the 600x520 dimensions -- confirmed by our own TOC
parser, not something that needs deeper oracle introspection. On top of
that, three colour channels give the RCT real cross-channel correlation to
find, same as 09/11's rationale, now spread across 9 groups instead of one.
cjxl printed nothing transform-specific at encode time; jxlinfo is not built
in this checkout; djxl -v / -v -v print no per-feature detail for this
stream. See 07_modular_gray_8x8_lossless.jxl.txt for the general caveat on
feature-introspection limits.

cjxl is used strictly as a BLACK BOX: it emits conformant streams for JPXL to
parse. libjxl's source is never read. If a rebuild at a different libjxl
revision changes these digests, that is the point of recording them -- do not
silently update them; note the revision change. As with 14, a different
group_dim heuristic in a future libjxl revision could make this fixture
single-section again -- tests/e2e_multisection.rs asserts `num_sections > 1`
so that regression is caught, not silently passed.
